currentContext.expansion: The annual report does not describe any greenfield manufacturing plant, capacity addition, or capex project with a commissioning timeline. Expansion is inorganic and structural rather than capacity-led. The Company acquired 100% of Vishal Personal Care Limited (VPCL) in two tranches: 49% (making VPCL an Associate Company w.e.f. March 10, 2025) and the remaining 51% during the financial year, making VPCL a wholly owned subsidiary w.e.f. May 16, 2025. VPCL operates two segments: (i) Manufacturing and Distribution of Consumer Products (skin care, body care and hair care) and (ii) Trademark Licensing and Other Business. To consolidate operations, the Board (July 24, 2025) approved a Scheme of Demerger transferring VPCL's Manufacturing and Distribution undertaking into Bajaj Consumer Care Limited on a going-concern basis with an appointed date of March 15, 2025, under Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act; the Scheme has received NCLT Jaipur approval and, being between a wholly owned subsidiary and parent, involves no share issuance or cash consideration. The residual trademark-licensing business remains with VPCL. Management expects the demerger to enable sharper business focus, drive operational synergies, improve resource utilisation, deliver cost efficiencies, enhance market reach and strengthen cash flows. The Company also completed a buyback during the year, extinguishing 64,34,482 equity shares (4.69% of paid-up capital) at INR 290 per share for an aggregate INR 18,660 lakh via the tender-offer route (opened Sept 11, closed Sept 17, 2025). Strategically, management points portfolio expansion toward premiumisation, value-added/enriched formats, natural/herbal formulations, D2C and omnichannel distribution, and quick-commerce channels within the hair oil and broader beauty & personal care categories.
currentContext.mdna: Moderation in core inflation coupled with stable input costs is expected to support margins across consumer-facing businesses|Gradual improvement in rural incomes and sentiment is likely to drive volume growth, especially in mass-market FMCG|FMCG value growth is mix-led, with pricing actions and premiumisation contributing more than sub-5% underlying volume growth|Rapid expansion of quick commerce (now one of the fastest-growing channels) is reshaping FMCG distribution and purchase behaviour|Shift toward branded, premium and health-oriented / natural and herbal formulations supports portfolio and premium-mix expansion|Organised retail and e-commerce continue to gain share, aided by GST 2.0 rationalisation improving affordability and pricing predictability|Gross margin expansion driven by disciplined revenue management, calibrated pricing, prudent cost optimisation and a favourable product mix|Hair oiling retains strong relevance in India via association with nourishment and scalp/hair health, with rural and semi-urban markets driving steady category growth

risks.risk: Macro-economic sensitivity and concentrated revenue base
risks.note: Input-cost inflation compresses profitability, an economic slowdown cuts consumer purchasing power, and over-dependence of sales on a few products/channels/geographies leaves top-line growth exposed; mitigated via monthly ExCom profitability reviews, NPD scale-up, M&A (Vishal Personal Care acquisition) and new international markets.

risks.risk: Shifting consumer preferences and rising competitive intensity
risks.note: Cultural, demographic and technology-driven shifts (natural/sustainable brands, premiumisation) plus new-age competitors in offline and online marketplaces threaten the core Hair Oil/ADHO franchise; addressed via U&A studies, brand-health tracking, three innovation pipelines (widening, premiumisation, disruption) and a TV-to-digital media shift.

Inadequate RM supply from disruptions, single-vendor dependency for RM/PM, and unfavourable price fluctuations can interrupt production; managed through biennial RM/PM risk assessments (next round Apr'26) and continuous commodity market monitoring.

risks.risk: Human resource attrition and succession gaps
risks.note: High attrition destabilises the organisation and weak succession planning for key roles threatens continuity; countered with connect programs (SAARATHI, townhalls, Chai pe Charcha), AARAMBH 90-day induction/buddy system for infant attrition, and development tracks (PACE, Shikhar, IDPs, IJPs).

Failure to comply with existing and emerging laws risks business continuity, reputation, penalties and damages; mitigated by consultant engagement across offices/plants/R&D/depots, periodic functional compliance reporting, and a statutory compliance automation tool planned for Q2 FY27 roll-out.

Breach or unauthorised IT access can disrupt operations, cause financial loss, brand damage, legal liability and leakage of IPRs/personal data; defences include 24x7 firewall threat detection (prevented a recent server attack), WAF, online/offline SAP backups, hardened SAP access controls (Jun'25) and periodic VAPT (next mid-FY27).

risks.risk: Operational disruption at plants and depots
risks.note: Accidents, fire incidents or strikes at company premises threaten employee safety, property and business continuity; managed via periodic internal/external safety assessments, a digitalised plant safety induction module, and periodic mock drills and safety training.

risks.risk: Brand and reputational risk from counterfeit products
risks.note: Counterfeiting, infringing and copycat products can erode brand equity and consumer trust, flagged as a distinct brand and reputational risk by management.

one-line thesis: Bajaj Consumer opened FY27 with a strong Q1 — ₹341cr revenue (+28% YoY), consolidated EBITDA doubling to ₹84.4cr (24.7% margin) — driven by ADHO low-teen MLH-adjusted volume growth, broad-based GT/OT strength in the "strong 20s", and a very strong international rebound. But the West Asia war spiked LLP/packaging/mustard/almond costs: gross margin slipped sequentially 63%→61.8% (still +510bps YoY), management flags Q2 as the tougher inflation quarter easing over Q3/Q4, and the current 24.7% EBITDA is at the top of its stated "low-to-mid 20s" aspiration — so the growth base resets down from here toward a "double-digit-to-low-teens" long-term rate.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | ₹341cr | +28% | Broad-based; GT & OT both "strong 20s"; rural grew in line with urban |
| EBITDA / margin | ₹84.4cr (consol) / 24.7% | ~2x (doubled) | Fixed-cost + employee savings >600bps vs Q1FY26; A&P held at 14.6% |
| PAT (rptd & normalized) | ₹70.7cr / 20.7% margin | — | Mgmt: "no significant one-offs" — only natural quarter-to-quarter cost skew |
| Gross margin | 61.8% | +510bps vs Q1FY26 | Down sequentially from 63% in Q4FY26 (raw-material spike) |
| Order book | n/a (FMCG) | — | — |
| Cash / net debt | not discussed | — | No debt or buyback/dividend commentary this call |
> ASP (consolidated) up 29% YoY. ADHO ≈ 80% of revenue; non-ADHO "growth portfolio" ≈ 15–20%; Banjara's ≈ 5% of revenue. Gross-margin drop is a raw-material story, not a mix or one-off distortion.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth:** No formal guidance ("we don't give guidances"). Q1's exponential growth is on a weak base and will "settle down to a slightly lower number" as those bases lap. **Long-term aspiration: consistent YoY double-digit to low-teens growth** — "we will be very disappointed / unhappy if we don't deliver double-digit growth in any quarter."
- **Gross margin:** Remains in a "tough zone" in Q2FY27 (slightly more under stress than Q1), then **expected to ease sequentially over Q3 and Q4 FY27** as high-cost inventory clears and spot prices cool. "Can't take margins for granted" in Q2.
- **EBITDA margin:** Aspiration to operate in the **"low to mid 20s"**; currently on the higher side of that. **No pricing actions planned** to drive further margin expansion; further gains depend only on operating leverage / topline flow-through.
- **Non-ADHO / growth portfolio:** Long term, aspire to **grow this portfolio in the "high 20s"**; the ~₹500cr growth-portfolio roadmap (set at Q4FY26, ~3yr horizon) is "progressing as per internal milestones" — detailed disclosure once a year.
- **Advertising:** Operate A&P in the **historical ~15–16% zone** over the medium term; "advertising is not an area where we are trying to squeeze on cost."
- **Project Aarohan:** ~**200–300bps one-time growth delta** per state on first execution (on a small mix); rolling out for the first time in **4 big states** this year; distribution expansion is a multi-year exercise thereafter.
- **Capex:** None discussed — distribution/brand-led model, no physical capex program.
- **M&A:** "Nothing to disclose" (asked twice).
order book & pipeline: Not applicable (FMCG). Forward demand read: momentum continuing into FY27; rural (recovered in H2FY26) now growing in line with urban; small packs / sachets leading ADHO volume; international channel rebuilt as a sustainable growth leg.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **ADHO (Almond Drops Hair Oil, ≈80% of revenue):** Low-teen volume growth on an **MLH-adjusted basis** (up from ~mid-single-digit prior quarters); growth broad-based across pack groups and channels; **small packs and sachets** the standout driver.
- **Non-ADHO "growth portfolio" (≈15–20%):** Grew high single-digit sequentially, improving run-rate — despite value deflation in coconut. **Coconut** is the largest piece; scale-up driven by distribution/availability, not free grammage. **Banjara's** (≈5% of revenue, held in VPC subsidiary) being revamped/repositioned — "most probably the second biggest, if not the biggest, leg" of the growth portfolio; pilots underway for disruptive growth ideas.
- **Channels:** GT and OT both grew in "strong 20s"; urban retail, wholesale and rural all strong; MT and e-commerce well; institutional business weak but <1% of mix.
- **International:** "Very, very strong rebound." Nepal & Bangladesh continued double-digit growth + margin improvement; **MENA** (challenged last year) very strong growth; **rest of world** (hit by tariffs last year) rebounded strongly — performance broad-based across countries.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Growth portfolio to ~₹500cr** (coconut + Banjara's + smaller brands), aspired to grow "high 20s"; diversification described as "more immediate on the agenda," not just coconut for 1–2 years.
- **Banjara's revamp** — repositioning + pilots; a formal "doubling-down" plan to be shared once ready.
- **International** as a newly-proven sustainable growth channel across geographies.
- **Project Aarohan** direct-distribution expansion — 4 new states this year plus continued deepening in existing states, building capability to carry a wider portfolio.
- **M&A optionality** — open but nothing to disclose; ₹500cr goal doesn't require acquisitions (could be a top-up).
margins & cost dynamics:
- Gross margin 63%→61.8% QoQ on **West Asia war** raw-material spike; still +510bps YoY.
- Cost drivers: **LLP and packaging** (petroleum-linked) extremely volatile; **mustard and almond** (edible oils) inflated and not easing in harvest season as usual; **copra** deflated off historic highs to ~₹130–135–140 range last couple of months (no normal seasonal cycle this year).
- Countermeasures: **selective/calibrated price increases + MLH (grammage) reduction** across the portfolio; A&P protected at 14.6%; **>600bps of savings** on fixed/employee/other-cost lines vs Q1FY26 via operating leverage.
- Overhang: **high-cost inventory** still in system; Q2 the tougher quarter, easing Q3/Q4 if spot prices cool.
- Coconut: discount to market leader deliberately rationalized over the past two years to a level that makes the portfolio profitable/sustainable; core hair-oil portfolio prices at a large premium to copra, so limited copra-price interplay.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): No physical capex program discussed. Investment is directed at **brand (A&P ~15–16%), digital/influencer marketing, and direct distribution (Project Aarohan, 4 new states)** — an opex/distribution-led expansion model rather than plant capex. No commissioning dates.
capital allocation:
- Priority: reinvest behind brands — A&P held ~14.6% this quarter, medium-term ~15–16%; significant spend on **influencer-led digital campaigns**; continued shift from traditional media to digital while maintaining SOV-SOM.
- Distribution investment via Project Aarohan.
- **M&A:** open but nothing to disclose; not required for the ₹500cr goal.
- No dividend / buyback / debt commentary this call.
risks & watch-items:
- **Input-cost inflation / war volatility** — LLP, packaging, mustard, almond; "very dynamic," war status uncertain ("couple of weeks back we thought the war is over… might not be so sure right now"); Q2 gross margin explicitly at risk.
- **High-cost inventory** working through the P&L into Q2.
- **Base effect** — exponential growth lapping strong bases from Q3FY26 onward; growth mathematically resets toward double-digit/low-teens.
- **Execution risk** named as the single largest risk to sustaining growth — future growth is largely market-share-gain-led, so distribution/execution slippage is the key threat.
- **Coconut / unorganized competition** post copra correction; competitive intensity in the value-added segments where Bajaj fights "extremely large competitors."
- **Guidance opacity** — management repeatedly declines quarterly/annual numeric guidance and limits non-ADHO disclosure (competitive sensitivity) to annual updates.
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined and unusually candid about uncertainty. Refuses to give numeric guidance but is precise on directionality (Q2 tough → Q3/Q4 ease; EBITDA at top of the low-to-mid-20s band; no pricing-led margin expansion). Proactively re-clarified an earlier remark to avoid implying cost-shifting between quarters. Sets a deliberately conservative long-term bar (double-digit-to-low-teens) while over-delivering near term, and frames execution/market-share as the real risk. Guards competitive data (non-ADHO, Banjara's) but promises annual disclosure cadence.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The 24.7% EBITDA / 20.7% PAT print is management's stated **ceiling zone**, not a launchpad — "pricing is not going to drive any further margin expansion," so upside from here is operating-leverage-only.
- ADHO volume acceleration (mid-single → low-teens) is driven by **small packs and sachets**, i.e. down-trading/affordability packs, not premium mix — a rural/value-led volume story.
- Coconut scale-up is **pure distribution-led**, explicitly "not giving any substantial free volume" — cleaner volume quality than a grammage-led push.
- Copra behaving abnormally (no seasonal inflation cycle this year) — a category signal worth tracking for all coconut-oil players.
- Aarohan's benefit is small in mix terms (200–300bps one-time on a small base) — the durable value is the multi-year "milk efficiency" of newly-added direct outlets, not the headline delta.
- Management sidestepped copra/unorganized dynamics in Kerala — "not very big markets for us," implicitly conceding the deep-South coconut belt to market leaders.

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.

identity.name: BAJAJ CONSUMER CARE LTD
identity.industry: FMCG / Hair Care & Personal Oil Brands

hero.oneLiner: Bajaj Consumer opened FY27 with a strong Q1, driven by ADHO low-teen MLH-adjusted volume growth, broad-based GT/OT strength in the "strong 20s", so the growth base resets down from here toward a "double-digit-to-low-teens" long-term rate.
hero.industry: FMCG / Hair Care & Personal Oil Brands

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Bajaj Consumer Care manufactures and sells personal care products spanning hair oils, skincare, lotions, soaps and haircare, with its flagship Bajaj Almond Drops hair oil at the core of the portfolio. The company serves Indian households through an extensive retail network and is extending its reach across domestic and international markets while broadening the portfolio into a holistic personal care play.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Uptown Properties and Leasing Private Limited — subsidiary: Indian wholly-owned subsidiary; 100% holding (unchanged from prior year)
- Bajaj Bangladesh Limited — subsidiary: Foreign subsidiary incorporated in Bangladesh; 100% holding
- Bajaj Corp International (FZE) — subsidiary: Foreign subsidiary incorporated in UAE; 100% holding
- Vishal Personal Care Limited — subsidiary: Indian personal care entity; became a wholly-owned subsidiary (100%) w.e.f. May 16, 2025, having earlier been a 49% associate
- Vishal Personal Care Limited — associate: Held as a 49% associate from March 10, 2025 to May 15, 2025 before becoming a subsidiary
- Bajaj Resources Private Limited (formerly Bajaj Resources Limited) — related party: Entity (including members of the same group) having significant influence over the reporting entity
- KNB Enterprises LLP — related party: Subsidiary of Bajaj Resources Private Limited

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **ADHO (Almond Drops Hair Oil, ≈80% of revenue):** Low-teen volume growth on an **MLH-adjusted basis** (up from ~mid-single-digit prior quarters); growth broad-based across pack groups and channels; **small packs and sachets** the standout driver.
- **Non-ADHO "growth portfolio" (≈15–20%):** Grew high single-digit sequentially, improving run-rate — despite value deflation in coconut. **Coconut** is the largest piece; scale-up driven by distribution/availability, not free grammage. **Banjara's** (≈5% of revenue, held in VPC subsidiary) being revamped/repositioned — "most probably the second biggest, if not the biggest, leg" of the growth portfolio; pilots underway for disruptive growth ideas.
- **Channels:** GT and OT both grew in "strong 20s"; urban retail, wholesale and rural all strong; MT and e-commerce well; institutional business weak but <1% of mix.
- **International:** "Very, very strong rebound." Nepal & Bangladesh continued double-digit growth + margin improvement; **MENA** (challenged last year) very strong growth; **rest of world** (hit by tariffs last year) rebounded strongly — performance broad-based across countries.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Hair Oil:** Bajaj Almond Drops, Almond Drops extensions
- **Personal Care:** Skincare products, Lotions, Soaps, Haircare solutions

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not applicable (FMCG). Forward demand read: momentum continuing into FY27; rural (recovered in H2FY26) now growing in line with urban; small packs / sachets leading ADHO volume; international channel rebuilt as a sustainable growth leg.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue growth:** No formal guidance ("we don't give guidances"). Q1's exponential growth is on a weak base and will "settle down to a slightly lower number" as those bases lap. **Long-term aspiration: consistent YoY double-digit to low-teens growth** — "we will be very disappointed / unhappy if we don't deliver double-digit growth in any quarter."
- **Gross margin:** Remains in a "tough zone" in Q2FY27 (slightly more under stress than Q1), then **expected to ease sequentially over Q3 and Q4 FY27** as high-cost inventory clears and spot prices cool. "Can't take margins for granted" in Q2.
- **EBITDA margin:** Aspiration to operate in the **"low to mid 20s"**; currently on the higher side of that. **No pricing actions planned** to drive further margin expansion; further gains depend only on operating leverage / topline flow-through.
- **Non-ADHO / growth portfolio:** Long term, aspire to **grow this portfolio in the "high 20s"**; the ~₹500cr growth-portfolio roadmap (set at Q4FY26, ~3yr horizon) is "progressing as per internal milestones" — detailed disclosure once a year.
- **Advertising:** Operate A&P in the **historical ~15–16% zone** over the medium term; "advertising is not an area where we are trying to squeeze on cost."
- **Project Aarohan:** ~**200–300bps one-time growth delta** per state on first execution (on a small mix); rolling out for the first time in **4 big states** this year; distribution expansion is a multi-year exercise thereafter.
- **Capex:** None discussed — distribution/brand-led model, no physical capex program.
- **M&A:** "Nothing to disclose" (asked twice).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Growth portfolio to ~₹500cr** (coconut + Banjara's + smaller brands), aspired to grow "high 20s"; diversification described as "more immediate on the agenda," not just coconut for 1–2 years.
- **Banjara's revamp** — repositioning + pilots; a formal "doubling-down" plan to be shared once ready.
- **International** as a newly-proven sustainable growth channel across geographies.
- **Project Aarohan** direct-distribution expansion — 4 new states this year plus continued deepening in existing states, building capability to carry a wider portfolio.
- **M&A optionality** — open but nothing to disclose; ₹500cr goal doesn't require acquisitions (could be a top-up).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Moderation in core inflation coupled with stable input costs is expected to support margins across consumer-facing businesses
- Gradual improvement in rural incomes and sentiment is likely to drive volume growth, especially in mass-market FMCG
- FMCG value growth is mix-led, with pricing actions and premiumisation contributing more than sub-5% underlying volume growth
- Rapid expansion of quick commerce (now one of the fastest-growing channels) is reshaping FMCG distribution and purchase behaviour
- Shift toward branded, premium and health-oriented / natural and herbal formulations supports portfolio and premium-mix expansion
- Organised retail and e-commerce continue to gain share, aided by GST 2.0 rationalisation improving affordability and pricing predictability
- Gross margin expansion driven by disciplined revenue management, calibrated pricing, prudent cost optimisation and a favourable product mix
- Hair oiling retains strong relevance in India via association with nourishment and scalp/hair health, with rural and semi-urban markets driving steady category growth

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- Gross margin 63%→61.8% QoQ on **West Asia war** raw-material spike; still +510bps YoY.
- Cost drivers: **LLP and packaging** (petroleum-linked) extremely volatile; **mustard and almond** (edible oils) inflated and not easing in harvest season as usual; **copra** deflated off historic highs to ~₹130–135–140 range last couple of months (no normal seasonal cycle this year).
- Countermeasures: **selective/calibrated price increases + MLH (grammage) reduction** across the portfolio; A&P protected at 14.6%; **>600bps of savings** on fixed/employee/other-cost lines vs Q1FY26 via operating leverage.
- Overhang: **high-cost inventory** still in system; Q2 the tougher quarter, easing Q3/Q4 if spot prices cool.
- Coconut: discount to market leader deliberately rationalized over the past two years to a level that makes the portfolio profitable/sustainable; core hair-oil portfolio prices at a large premium to copra, so limited copra-price interplay.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Priority: reinvest behind brands — A&P held ~14.6% this quarter, medium-term ~15–16%; significant spend on **influencer-led digital campaigns**; continued shift from traditional media to digital while maintaining SOV-SOM.
- Distribution investment via Project Aarohan.
- **M&A:** open but nothing to disclose; not required for the ₹500cr goal.
- No dividend / buyback / debt commentary this call.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report does not describe any greenfield manufacturing plant, capacity addition, or capex project with a commissioning timeline. Expansion is inorganic and structural rather than capacity-led. The Company acquired 100% of Vishal Personal Care Limited (VPCL) in two tranches: 49% (making VPCL an Associate Company w.e.f. March 10, 2025) and the remaining 51% during the financial year, making VPCL a wholly owned subsidiary w.e.f. May 16, 2025. VPCL operates two segments: (i) Manufacturing and Distribution of Consumer Products (skin care, body care and hair care) and (ii) Trademark Licensing and Other Business. To consolidate operations, the Board (July 24, 2025) approved a Scheme of Demerger transferring VPCL's Manufacturing and Distribution undertaking into Bajaj Consumer Care Limited on a going-concern basis with an appointed date of March 15, 2025, under Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act; the Scheme has received NCLT Jaipur approval and, being between a wholly owned subsidiary and parent, involves no share issuance or cash consideration. The residual trademark-licensing business remains with VPCL. Management expects the demerger to enable sharper business focus, drive operational synergies, improve resource utilisation, deliver cost efficiencies, enhance market reach and strengthen cash flows. The Company also completed a buyback during the year, extinguishing 64,34,482 equity shares (4.69% of paid-up capital) at INR 290 per share for an aggregate INR 18,660 lakh via the tender-offer route (opened Sept 11, closed Sept 17, 2025). Strategically, management points portfolio expansion toward premiumisation, value-added/enriched formats, natural/herbal formulations, D2C and omnichannel distribution, and quick-commerce channels within the hair oil and broader beauty & personal care categories.
